title: LeCellModel: Interpretable Density Estimation over the Gene Expression Manifold
claim: A single encoder-projector backbone is trained with adversarial, predictive, and auxiliary losses, and its outputs serve downstream tasks directly.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right main chain, branches up and down, dashed training box
description: A single block diagram inside a dashed rounded box labeled 'Training'. A horizontal main chain runs left to right. It starts at input x (blue), then Global/local views (blue), then Encoder f_theta with representation z in R^d (gray), then Projector g_phi with projection p in R^k (gray). An arrow leaves the projector to a gray 'Downstream tasks' box outside the dashed region. Two solid arrows branch upward. One goes from the encoder through a purple GRL box to a green 'Batch adversary L_adv' box. The other goes from the projector to a green 'Prediction + SIGReg L_pred + L_sig' box. A dashed lower path runs from x through 'Sparse gene perturbation' (blue) to a purple 'Displacement aux. L_disp' box, which also receives a dashed arrow from the projector. Colors separate inputs, backbone, losses and auxiliary modules. The eye starts at the central chain.
caption: Overview of LeCellModel. Input cells are augmented into global and local views. The encoder $f_\theta$ maps each view to a representation $z \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and the projector $g_\phi$ maps $z$ to a projection $p \in \mathbb{R}^k$. During training, batch supervision acts on $z$ through an explicit gradient-reversal layer (GRL), JEPA prediction and SIGReg regularization act on $p$, and an optional displacement auxiliary predicts projection shifts induced by sparse gene-space perturbations applied to the input cell. The projection $p$ can be used directly as an embedding for downstream tasks, while the JEPA-score is computed separately from the Jacobian of $F=g_\phi\circ f_\theta$.
abstract: Representation learning for single-cell RNA-seq has been evaluated by the identities representations capture -- cell types, lineages, perturbations -- rather than how faithfully they model the distribution of cell states on the gene expression manifold. As a result, density estimation, rare-state detection, perturbation scoring, and gene-level attribution are bolted onto frozen embeddings as separate models, disconnected from the geometry of the data. We argue that modeling the distribution of cell states should be the primary objective, and that representation quality follows from it. Building on LeJEPA, whose SIGReg objective enforces a provably optimal isotropic Gaussian latent, we introduce LeCellModel, which reads the encoder's Jacobian log-volume (JEPA-SCORE) under this Gaussian latent as a relative typicality score. Across several datasets, LeCellModel outperforms established methods on the scIB benchmark for representation quality. Furthermore, we show that LeCellModel enables detection of rare expression states using JEPA-SCORE as a typicality measure, applying it to a controlled cytokine panel, where it identifies stimulated cells across minority fractions and tracks pathway-response magnitude. We introduce gene-level interpretability of the typicality score -- to our knowledge, the first method for analyzing JEPA-SCORE in feature space. Leveraging this framework, LeCellModel recapitulates the known association of a profibrotic macrophage program with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and discovers a CD177+ activated regulatory T cell subpopulation previously described only in tumor contexts. Both findings emerge directly from the geometry of the learned embedding, without relying on supervised annotations.
